card.name: Points where a legend or tale is about to be told
card.fires_on: Small words or punctuation right before a traditional tale or anecdote is told, such as "legend has it", "it is said that" or "as recorded by". It appears in history and folklore passages about famous people and places.

modes.label: Legend lead-in
modes.description: Linking words or the word legend just before a story is retold.
modes.example: Moaning Cavern was rediscovered in 1919, and<< legend>> has it that tourists were lowered into the

modes.label: Hearsay attribution
modes.description: Words like "is" or "as" that start a reported saying or ancient record.

modes.label: End of a story setup
modes.description: Punctuation after a sentence that introduces a legendary anecdote, where the tale comes next.
modes.example: One legendary anecdote from Lincoln's early life was that of the cherry tree growing alongside the Lincoln family log cabin<<.>> One

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict story, legend and tale words next.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a history text where a legend or traditional story is about to be told.
